blocks.text: Imagine you're juggling several balls. Each time you catch one, you must remember its position and speed before moving to the next. This is akin to what an operating system does during context switching.

blocks.markdown: In operating systems, context switching is the process of storing the state of a process or thread so that it can be resumed later. This is crucial for multitasking, allowing multiple processes to share a single CPU.

blocks.title: Context Switching
blocks.text: Context switching is the mechanism by which an operating system switches the CPU from executing one process to executing another by saving and restoring the state of processes.

blocks.markdown: During a context switch, the operating system must save the current state of the process being switched out and load the state of the process being switched in. This involves saving and restoring various elements of the process state.

blocks.title: State Components in Context Switching
blocks.text: The state saved during a context switch typically includes the program counter, CPU registers, and memory management information.

blocks.caption: Components of process state saved during a context switch.

blocks.title: Example of Context Switching
blocks.prompt: Consider a CPU switching from Process A to Process B. Describe the steps involved in this context switch.

steps.text: Save the state of Process A.
steps.latex: 1. \text{Save PC, registers, and memory info of Process A.}

steps.text: Load the state of Process B.
steps.latex: 2. \text{Load PC, registers, and memory info of Process B.}

steps.text: Update the CPU to execute Process B.
steps.latex: 3. \text{Set CPU to start executing instructions from Process B's PC.}

blocks.answer: The context switch involves saving Process A's state and loading Process B's state, allowing the CPU to execute Process B.

blocks.markdown: Context switching is not free; it incurs a measurable cost in terms of time and system resources. This cost arises from the overhead of saving and restoring process states.

blocks.title: Cost of Context Switching
blocks.text: Excessive context switching can degrade system performance due to the overhead involved in saving and restoring process states.

blocks.title: Cost Comparison: Thread vs. Process Switch
blocks.prompt: Compare the cost of switching between threads and switching between processes.

steps.text: Identify the state saved in a thread switch.
steps.latex: 1. \text{Save PC and registers for thread switch.}

steps.text: Identify the state saved in a process switch.
steps.latex: 2. \text{Save PC, registers, and memory info for process switch.}
3. \text{Thread switch is less costly than process switch due to fewer state components.}

blocks.answer: Thread switching is generally less costly than process switching because it involves saving and restoring fewer components.

points: Context switching involves saving and restoring the state of processes or threads.
The cost of context switching is significant and can affect system performance.
Thread switches are generally less costly than process switches.
